newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Banker urges Australia to repair image in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Banker urges Australia to repair image in Asia.

text.p: A senior investment banker on Monday urged Australia to fix its damaged image in Asia and said the nation's race debate had left Canberra with a big "repair job" to do.

Trevor Rowe, Asia-Pacific chief executive for U.S. investment bank Salomon Brothers Inc, said Australia's political and business leaders failed to respond quickly to the emergence last year of a backlash against Asian immigration.
"I think there is a repair job to do," Rowe told Reuters after addressing a business luncheon in Melbourne.
The backlash, led by race row politician Pauline Hanson, has been cited as a threat to Australia's trade and investment links with Asia by the government and business alike.
But Rowe said government and business leaders had themselves to blame for the damaging publicity given in Asia to the comments of Hanson, leader of the far-right One Nation party.
"I think our business and political leadership failed last year to stand up vigorously at the time when she gave her maiden speech (to parliament)," he told the luncheon.
"That sort of seemed to imply some sort of acceptance of those views."
Hanson has called for a freeze on immigration, arguing in her first speech to parliament that Australia was in danger of being "swamped by Asians".
The Australian government has in recent months stepped up its criticism of Hanson, describing her views as stupid.
But Rowe, who is based in Hong Kong, said Canberra's decision this month to slash the nation's annual immigrant intake did nothing to improve Australia's tarnished image.
"Everywhere I go, I get asked these damn questions (about racism in Australia)," Australian-born Rowe told the luncheon. "Australia annoys the hell out of me."
